Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: Which of the following statements best describes the main outcome of carrying out critical path analysis on a project?
o: It documents the change requests raised during delivery
It assigns responsibilities using a RACI matrix
It calculates the financial return forecast for the project
It identifies which activities directly control the project duration
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: Critical path analysis identifies the activities that control the overall duration, distinguishing them from those with float.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: How does critical path analysis help a project manager decide where to concentrate limited resources?
o: By highlighting the activities that cannot afford to slip
By ranking stakeholders according to their influence
By showing which activities have the greatest cost
By listing the risks with the highest impact scores
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: By highlighting zero-float activities, critical path analysis shows where resources must be protected to avoid delaying the project.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: A critical activity is forecast to overrun by two days. According to critical path analysis, what is the likely effect?
o: The project end date slips by two days unless recovered
The project end date is unaffected because of float
The project baseline automatically re-sets itself
Only non-critical activities are delayed by two days
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: A slip on a zero-float critical activity pushes out the project completion date unless corrective action recovers the time.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: Which of the following is NOT a purpose of critical path analysis?
o: Identifying the longest sequence of dependent activities
Justifying the project's investment to the sponsor
Determining the shortest possible project duration
Revealing which activities have float available
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: Critical path analysis addresses scheduling, not investment justification, which is the role of the business case.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: What is the main purpose of critical path analysis within a project schedule?
o: To identify the sequence of activities that determines the shortest project duration
To distribute resources evenly across all of the project's activities
To define the roles and responsibilities of the project team
To estimate the project's costs from comparable past projects
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: Critical path analysis identifies the longest chain of dependent activities, which sets the minimum overall duration of the project.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: What does resource levelling involve when a project schedule shows its resources to be over-allocated?
o: Adjusting activity dates so demand does not exceed availability, even if the end date moves
Increasing the budget so additional resources can be hired immediately
Scheduling all activities in parallel so resources are used at once
Reducing the project's scope so the existing resources become sufficient
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: Resource levelling reschedules activities to keep demand within available resource limits, and may extend the project end date to do so.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: Which resource optimisation technique evens out resource usage by delaying tasks only within their available float?
o: Critical path analysis
Resource smoothing
Schedule crashing
Resource levelling
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: Resource smoothing delays activities within their float to even out resource usage while keeping the critical path and end date unchanged.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: Which document sets out a project's approach to sourcing, including make-or-buy decisions and contract types?
o: Procurement strategy
Quality plan
Risk register
Communication plan
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: The procurement strategy defines how goods and services will be sourced, covering make-or-buy analysis, contract types and supplier selection.

Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.q: What does the term 'time boxing' mean in the context of project scheduling?
o: Assigning the most skilled resources to the highest-priority activities first
Decomposing the project's work into smaller and more manageable packages
Estimating durations by comparing them with similar completed activities
Fixing a set duration for an activity or phase and completing what is possible within it
Resource, Scheduling & Optimisation.w: Time boxing allocates a fixed, unmovable period to an activity or phase, focusing effort on what can be achieved within that time.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement best defines a 'risk' in the context of project management?
o: A confirmed problem that requires immediate resolution by the team
An uncertain event that, should it occur, would affect the project's objectives
A completed task that is currently waiting for formal approval
A cost overrun that has already occurred and cannot be recovered
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is an uncertain future event that may have a positive or negative effect on project objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following best illustrates a risk on a project?
o: The project sponsor has already resigned from their post
A key supplier has already defaulted on an agreed delivery
The team has already exceeded the budget agreed for the phase
Adverse weather could delay the construction work later in the year
Risk & Issue Management.w: Adverse weather is an uncertain future event that may delay delivery, so it is a risk; the others have already happened and are issues.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does a 'risk' differ from a 'certainty' in project management terms?
o: A risk lies outside the manager's control, whereas a certainty does not
A risk concerns team behaviour, whereas a certainty concerns the sponsor
A risk involves uncertainty, whereas a certainty does not
A risk always leads to failure, whereas a certainty leads to success
Risk & Issue Management.w: The defining feature of a risk is uncertainty: it may or may not occur, unlike a certainty.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following would NOT be classed as a project risk?
o: Potential cost savings from adopting a new item of technology
Confirmed damage that has already occurred to a delivery vehicle
Expected delays caused by forthcoming changes in legislation
Possible supplier delays arising from future industrial action
Risk & Issue Management.w: A confirmed event that has already happened is a current issue, not an uncertain future event, so it is not a risk.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What characteristic must an event have before it can be classed as a project risk?
o: It must be uncertain and capable of affecting the project's objectives
It must lie entirely outside the project team's ability to control
It must occur only during the execution phase of the project
It must be guaranteed to happen at some point during the project
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk must be uncertain and able to affect objectives, whether positively or negatively.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why is risk management important to the successful delivery of a project?
o: It ensures that all project issues are completely avoided altogether
It guarantees that the project will succeed and meet every objective
It removes the need for stakeholders to be involved in the project
It allows uncertainties to be identified and controlled before they occur
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management enables uncertainties that could affect objectives to be identified, assessed and responded to proactively.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager maintains a risk register and reviews it each week. How does this best support project success?
o: It removes all remaining assumptions from the project management plan
It allows risks to be monitored continuously and responses to be actioned
It ensures the lessons learned are all documented before work begins
It prevents any further change requests from being raised during delivery
Risk & Issue Management.w: Regular review of the risk register lets the team act on emerging threats and opportunities before they escalate.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A risk plan notes that poor weather may delay construction. What benefit does identifying this early provide?
o: It removes the impact of every environmental risk on the project
It gives the team time to prepare responses before any delay occurs
It removes the need for configuration control during the project
It guarantees that the project will remain within its agreed scope
Risk & Issue Management.w: Identifying risks early is the purpose of risk management: it allows responses to be planned before problems arise.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A team recognises that a supplier might fail to meet its deadlines. Which stage of risk management does this demonstrate?
o: Risk identification
Risk acceptance
Risk avoidance
Risk exploitation
Risk & Issue Management.w: Spotting a potential future threat before it materialises is an example of risk identification.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does effective risk management support communication within a project?
o: It removes the need to hold regular project team meetings
It removes the need to hold a contingency budget in reserve
It gives the team a shared understanding of potential challenges and responses
It allows difficult decisions to be deferred until project closure
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management aligns the team around known uncertainties and agreed responses, supporting open and transparent communication.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the primary purpose of the risk identification stage?
o: To capture and record potential future events that may affect objectives
To assign risk owners and set aside their mitigation budgets
To resolve every open issue before project execution begins
To remove all uncertainty from the project management plan
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk identification focuses on uncovering and recording potential future events that could affect the project's objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A team holds a brainstorming session to work out what could prevent successful delivery. Which risk management stage is this?
o: Risk analysis
Risk response
Risk closure
Risk identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: Brainstorming is a common technique used during risk identification to surface possible risks.

Risk & Issue Management.q: During which stage would a project manager draw on lessons learned from earlier projects to spot potential risks?
o: Risk acceptance
Risk response
Risk closure
Risk identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: Lessons learned from previous projects are a useful input to risk identification, helping surface recurring or overlooked risks.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following is commonly used as a tool for identifying project risks?
o: Critical path analysis, identifying the longest sequence of activities
SWOT analysis, examining strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats
Earned value analysis, comparing planned and actual project performance
MoSCoW prioritisation, ranking requirements by their relative importance
Risk & Issue Management.w: SWOT analysis is a recognised technique during the identification stage of the risk management process for surfacing threats and opportunities.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project team recognises potential cyber-attacks as a threat to delivery. What has this activity achieved?
o: It has identified a risk
It has closed the risk
It has analysed the risk's impact
It has accepted the risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: Recognising cyber-attacks as a possible future threat means the team has successfully identified a risk.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the main objective of risk analysis in project management?
o: To approve outstanding change requests more quickly
To assess the likelihood and impact of each identified risk
To transfer every identified risk to external suppliers
To remove all uncertainty from the project's plans
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk analysis evaluates how likely each identified risk is to occur and how much it would affect the project's objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project team uses a probability and impact matrix to assess its risks. What are they doing?
o: Creating the risk register
Performing risk analysis
Prioritising the lessons learned
Carrying out risk identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: A probability and impact matrix is a standard method of carrying out qualitative risk analysis.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A high-impact, low-probability risk has been identified. What should risk analysis then help the team decide?
o: Whether to accept, avoid, reduce or transfer it as the response
Whether to delay the whole project until the threat has passed
Whether to ignore the risk simply because it is unlikely to occur
Whether to remove the affected deliverable from the project
Risk & Issue Management.w: Analysis of likelihood and impact informs the choice of an appropriate response, such as accept, avoid, reduce or transfer.

Risk & Issue Management.q: In quantitative risk analysis, which technique might a team use to simulate many possible risk outcomes?
o: The Delphi technique
MoSCoW prioritisation
An Ishikawa diagram
Monte Carlo simulation
Risk & Issue Management.w: Monte Carlo simulation is a quantitative technique that models many scenarios to estimate the range of likely outcomes.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A team colour-codes its risks red, amber and green to show their severity. What is this an example of?
o: Qualitative risk analysis
Quantitative risk analysis
Configuration management
Critical path analysis
Risk & Issue Management.w: Ranking risks by descriptive categories such as red, amber and green is a form of qualitative risk analysis.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager prepares a backup supplier agreement, to be used only if the main vendor fails to deliver. What is this arrangement best called?
o: A contingency reserve
A transfer response
A fallback plan
An avoidance response
Risk & Issue Management.w: A fallback plan is a plan B, put into action only if the risk occurs. Here the backup supplier is used only if the main vendor fails.

n.0: A contingency reserve is an amount of time or money set aside for risk, not an alternative course of action.
n.1: Transfer passes the financial impact or management of the risk to a third party, for example through insurance or a contract.
n.3: Avoidance changes the plan so the threat cannot happen; the risk of the vendor failing still remains here.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following is an example of the risk response known as avoidance?
o: Removing a high-risk feature from the project's scope entirely
Accepting the possibility of a small delay to final delivery
Buying insurance to cover possible damage to project equipment
Increasing the budget to cope with late supplier deliveries
Risk & Issue Management.w: Avoidance removes the threat completely, for example by taking the risky element out of scope.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A team decides to take no pre-emptive action against a possible delay to key components. Which risk response is this?
o: Transfer
Acceptance
Avoidance
Mitigation
Risk & Issue Management.w: Acceptance means acknowledging a risk and taking no pre-emptive action unless it actually materialises.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the purpose of producing a risk response plan?
o: To document the acceptance criteria for the project's final deliverables
To define how the team will react once issues have been logged
To develop the project's work breakdown structure
To set out the actions that will reduce, avoid, transfer or accept each risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk response plan records the agreed action for each risk, whether to reduce, avoid, transfer or accept it.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project passes a risky component to a specialist third party under contract. Which risk response is being used?
o: Acceptance
Mitigation
Transfer
Avoidance
Risk & Issue Management.w: Transfer shifts responsibility for a risk to another party, commonly through a contract or insurance.

Risk & Issue Management.q: When should a project risk normally be formally closed?
o: At the very start of the project's initiation stage
When it is no longer relevant or has been fully addressed
Only after the post-project review has taken place
As soon as it has first been identified by the team
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is closed once it no longer poses a threat or opportunity, whether through response or expiry.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A regulatory change that was once a major risk is now confirmed not to apply to the project. What should happen?
o: The risk should be re-analysed and given a new impact score
The risk should be formally closed in the risk register
The risk should be transferred to the project sponsor
The risk should be reprioritised as a high-impact risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: As the threat no longer applies, the risk should be formally closed and recorded in the register.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why is it important to formally close risks during the risk management process?
o: To prevent risks from being escalated to the project’s stakeholders
To keep the risk register accurate and focused on active threats
To transfer the lessons learned directly into the project issue log
To reduce the number of meetings the project team must hold
Risk & Issue Management.w: Closure removes risks that are no longer relevant, keeping the risk register current and focused on active threats and opportunities.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A supplier-capacity risk has been successfully dealt with through earlier delivery. What should the project manager do next?
o: Close the risk and record its outcome in the register
Leave the risk open in case the problem returns later
Remove the supplier from the project altogether
Escalate the risk to the project sponsor for a decision
Risk & Issue Management.w: Once a risk has been resolved it should be closed and its outcome documented to keep the register accurate.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which action is most appropriate during the risk closure stage of the risk management process?
o: Reviewing the outcomes and updating the lessons learned
Increasing the project's contingency budget for reassurance
Converting each closed risk into a formal change request
Assigning new owners to risks that have already expired
Risk & Issue Management.w: Closure involves recording outcomes and capturing lessons learned to improve risk handling on future projects.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the primary purpose of a risk register in project management?
o: To record and manage identified risks and their planned responses
To record the availability of staff across the project
To maintain the project's formal change control log
To monitor the day-to-day tasks of the project team
Risk & Issue Management.w: The risk register is the tool used to document identified risks, their status and their planned responses.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager revises the likelihood rating of an existing risk after new information arrives. Where is this recorded?
o: In the project issue log
In the stakeholder register
In the risk register
In the schedule baseline
Risk & Issue Management.w: The risk register is kept up to date throughout the project to reflect changes in likelihood, impact and status.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A high-impact risk was reduced by early action, and the manager records this in the register. Why does this matter?
o: It automatically triggers a review of the team's performance
It provides an audit trail of the risk treatment actions taken
It ensures the stakeholder matrix is kept fully up to date
It activates a formal contract change notice with suppliers
Risk & Issue Management.w: Recording responses and their outcomes in the register provides transparency and an audit trail that supports future learning.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following would you NOT normally expect to find recorded in a risk register?
o: The actual durations recorded for completed project tasks
A clear description of each identified risk
The probability and impact scores for each risk
The named person who owns each identified risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: Actual task durations belong to the schedule, not the risk register, which focuses on uncertainty and responses.

Risk & Issue Management.q: During a project review, the sponsor asks for an overview of the project's current risks and how each is being managed. Which document should the project manager present?
o: The business case
The product breakdown structure
The project schedule
The risk register
Risk & Issue Management.w: The risk register is the central record of identified risks, their assessed severity, planned responses and current status, making it the correct document for reviewing how risks are being managed.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following best defines a project issue in APM terms?
o: A problem breaching tolerance that needs the sponsor to help resolve it
A possible delay that could arise later during the deployment phase
An uncertain event that may affect the project's objectives in the future
A threat for which a reduction response must be planned in advance
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is a problem that is breaching, or about to breach, the delegated tolerances and needs the sponsor's support to agree a resolution. It has happened, so it is certain.

n.1: A possible future delay is uncertain, so it is a risk rather than an issue.
n.2: An uncertain future event is the definition of a risk.
n.3: Planning a response to a threat is risk management; the threat has not yet happened.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project's main server crashes, halting all progress. How should this event most accurately be classified?
o: As a risk, because it may affect the schedule
As a constraint, because it limits progress
As a milestone, because it marks an event
As an issue, because it has already occurred
Risk & Issue Management.w: The crash has already happened and is affecting delivery, so it is an issue to be managed and resolved rather than an uncertain future risk.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement best describes the difference in timing between an issue and a risk?
o: An issue is a future possibility, whereas a risk is a current event
An issue is a current or past event, whereas a risk is a future possibility
Both an issue and a risk describe events that may occur in future
Both an issue and a risk describe events that have already occurred
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is a present or past event requiring resolution, while a risk is an uncertain event that has not yet occurred.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A defect is found that stops key features working and will push delivery beyond the time tolerance agreed with the sponsor. How should the project manager treat it?
o: As a risk, because it might affect the project later
As a change request, because the scope has now altered
As an issue, as it has occurred and breaches tolerance
As a constraint, because it now limits the design
Risk & Issue Management.w: The defect has already happened and breaches the agreed time tolerance, so it is an issue to be logged, assessed and escalated to the sponsor.

n.0: A risk is uncertain and in the future, whereas this defect is already affecting delivery.
n.1: The scope has not been changed; a change request may follow from the agreed resolution, but the problem itself is an issue.
n.3: A constraint is a limit set on the project, not a problem that has arisen during it.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement correctly describes a project issue?
o: It is a problem now exceeding tolerances and needing escalation
It is an uncertainty relating to the project business case
It is a scheduled event that is recorded in the risk register
It is a constraint that has been imposed by the project sponsor
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is a problem that is breaching, or about to breach, delegated tolerances, so it is escalated to the sponsor to agree a resolution.

n.1: An uncertainty is a risk; an issue is certain because it is already happening.
n.2: Issues are unplanned and recorded in the issue log, not scheduled events in the risk register.
n.3: A constraint is a limit placed on the project, not a problem that has arisen.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the primary purpose of issue management within a project?
o: To develop contingency plans for anticipated external risks
To estimate the overall duration of the project's activities
To record, evaluate and resolve events that have already occurred
To identify and assess possible future threats to the project
Risk & Issue Management.w: Issue management provides a structured approach to capturing, assessing and resolving events that have already happened during the project.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A supplier fails to deliver components on time, delaying the schedule. What is the role of issue management in this situation?
o: To revise the scope so the affected tasks are removed
To document the issue, assign ownership and track its resolution
To plan the resources needed for the next project phase
To reassess the project's future risks and update tolerances
Risk & Issue Management.w: Issue management handles real disruptions such as a missed delivery by logging them, assigning an owner and tracking them through to resolution.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does effective issue management benefit a project?
o: It helps maintain control and minimise disruption to delivery
It removes the need for a formal change control process
It guarantees that every deliverable will meet its specification
It eliminates all remaining risks from the project entirely
Risk & Issue Management.w: By recording and resolving problems promptly, issue management reduces their impact and helps keep the project under control.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A key stakeholder's objection has halted work on site, and the resulting delay now exceeds the project manager's tolerance. Which process should be used to handle this?
o: Scope management
Risk identification
Configuration management
Issue management
Risk & Issue Management.w: The problem has happened and breaches tolerance, so it is an issue: it is logged, assessed, escalated to the sponsor and resolved through issue management.

n.0: Scope management identifies, defines and controls outputs, outcomes and benefits; it does not handle this problem.
n.1: Risk identification deals with uncertain future events, but this has already happened.
n.2: Configuration management controls and records versions of items, not stakeholder problems.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following is NOT typically part of the issue management process?
o: Scoring the probability and impact of the issue before it occurs
Monitoring progress until the issue is resolved and then closed
Recording the issue within a formal issue register or log
Assigning a named owner to take responsibility for the issue
Risk & Issue Management.w: Scoring probability and impact belongs to risk management; an issue has already occurred, so it is logged, owned, resolved and closed.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following best describes the difference between an issue and a risk?
o: A risk relates to cost, whereas an issue relates to quality
A risk must be escalated, whereas an issue does not
A risk is recorded in the schedule, whereas an issue is not
A risk is a future uncertainty, whereas an issue is a current problem
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is an uncertain future event, while an issue is a problem that has already occurred and must be resolved.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A possible delay to delivery is identified because a supplier may be overloaded with work. How should this be classified?
o: As a milestone, because it marks a delivery point
As a risk, because it has not yet happened
As a change request, because the plan must alter
As an issue, because it is affecting the project now
Risk & Issue Management.w: The delay is only a possibility that has not yet occurred, so it is an uncertain future event and is therefore a risk.

Risk & Issue Management.q: During testing, a defect is found that prevents deployment and cannot be fixed within the project manager's delegated tolerances. How should it be classified?
o: As an issue, because it has occurred and breaches tolerance
As a risk, because it may affect deployment later
As a baseline, because it defines the tested product
As an assumption, because defects were expected during testing
Risk & Issue Management.w: The defect has already happened and cannot be resolved within delegated tolerances, which is exactly what an issue is. It is escalated to the sponsor.

n.1: A risk is an uncertain future event; this defect is already blocking deployment.
n.2: A baseline is the agreed plan against which progress is measured, not a problem.
n.3: An assumption is something taken to be true for planning; a blocking defect is a real problem.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the key difference in timing between issues and risks?
o: Both issues and risks relate only to events after project delivery
Risks relate to the future, whereas issues occur in the present or past
Both issues and risks are recorded only once lessons are learned
Issues relate to the future, whereas risks occur in the present or past
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risks are anticipated future events, whereas issues are events that have already happened and are affecting the project.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A developer flags a design flaw that could delay testing if it is not addressed. How should this be managed?
o: Record it in the risk register, as it is a possible future event
Add it to the work breakdown structure as a new task
Escalate it immediately to the project sponsor for a decision
Record it in the issue register, as it has already occurred
Risk & Issue Management.w: Because the delay has not yet happened and would only occur if the flaw is not addressed, it is an uncertain future event and belongs in the risk register.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement correctly reflects the relationship between a risk and an issue on a project?
o: A risk is always a negative event that will harm the project
A risk and an issue are always recorded within the same register
An issue can always be prevented through effective mitigation planning
An issue represents a realised risk or a newly arising problem
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is something that has happened now, arising either from a risk that has materialised or from a new event, unlike a risk which is uncertain.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A key risk recorded in the project's risk register has now materialised. What should happen next?
o: It should be ignored because it has already been analysed
It should be closed and recorded as a completed milestone
It should be deleted from the risk register without further action
It should be reclassified as an issue and managed accordingly
Risk & Issue Management.w: Once a risk actually occurs it becomes a current problem, so it is reclassified as an issue and handled through the issue management process.

Risk & Issue Management.q: An issue has occurred within a project. Which process is used to resolve it?
o: Configuration management
Change control
Issue management
Risk management
Risk & Issue Management.w: Issue management is the structured process for recording, assessing and resolving problems once they have occurred.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following is NOT typically part of the issue management process?
o: Scoring the probability and impact of the event
Logging the event in a formal issue register
Closing the event once it has been resolved
Assigning an owner to manage the event
Risk & Issue Management.w: Scoring probability and impact belongs to risk management, because issues have already occurred and so their likelihood is no longer uncertain.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why are risks and issues typically tracked separately on a project?
o: Risk tracking is optional, whereas issue tracking is mandatory
Issues must always be resolved before the project can start
They follow different lifecycles and require different treatment
Only risks can be escalated to senior management for a decision
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risks are analysed and planned for as uncertain future events, while issues are resolved as current problems, so they need separate processes and records.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is normally the first step in a typical issue resolution process?
o: Escalating the issue directly to the project board
Closing the issue as soon as it has been recorded
Implementing a resolution before any assessment is made
Identifying and logging the issue in the issue register
Risk & Issue Management.w: The issue must first be identified and formally logged so that it can then be assessed, owned and tracked to resolution.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A supplier misses a key delivery, so the project manager records it and assigns it to the procurement lead. Which stage of issue resolution is this?
o: Analysis of the issue's impact on objectives
Identification and assignment of the issue
Closure of the issue once it is verified
Resolution of the issue through corrective action
Risk & Issue Management.w: Logging the issue and giving it an owner are part of the initial identification and assignment stage of the resolution process.

Risk & Issue Management.q: During which stage of the issue resolution process is the effect of the issue on the project's objectives determined?
o: Assess the impact
Track to closure
Agree the resolution
Identify and log
Risk & Issue Management.w: After the issue is identified and logged, its impact on the objectives is assessed so the sponsor has the information needed when it is escalated.

n.1: Tracking to closure monitors the agreed actions until the issue is resolved.
n.2: The resolution is agreed after the impact has been assessed and the issue escalated.
n.3: Identifying and logging records the issue; its impact is worked out in the next stage.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A software defect has been fixed, tested and verified. What is the final step in the issue resolution process?
o: Escalation of the issue to a higher authority
Closure of the issue, recording it as complete
Reassessment of the issue's potential impact
Reopening the issue for further investigation
Risk & Issue Management.w: Once an issue has been resolved and verified, it is formally closed and recorded as complete.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following best describes the escalation step in the issue resolution process?
o: Recording the lessons learned after the issue is resolved
Logging the issue formally when it is first identified
Raising the issue beyond project authority for a decision
Assigning the issue to a stakeholder for resolution
Risk & Issue Management.w: Escalation is used when an issue exceeds the project manager's authority and requires a decision from a higher level of governance.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project's main server crashes during a product launch. What should the project manager do first?
o: Replace the server without recording what happened
Log the issue and assess its impact on the project
Escalate the problem straight to the project sponsor
Cancel the launch until the server is restored
Risk & Issue Management.w: The first step is to formally log the issue and assess its impact so that an informed decision on the response can be made.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is typically carried out during the resolution step of the issue management process?
o: Assigning the issue to a responsible team member
Determining the overall severity of the issue
Recording the issue formally in the register
Taking corrective action to resolve the issue
Risk & Issue Management.w: The resolution step involves implementing the planned corrective action to deal with and close out the issue.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which sequence correctly shows the main stages of the issue resolution process?
o: Log, escalate to sponsor, assess, agree resolution, track to closure
Log, assess, agree resolution, escalate to sponsor, track to closure
Log, assess, escalate to sponsor, agree resolution, track to closure
Assess, log, escalate to sponsor, track to closure, agree resolution
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is identified and logged, its impact is assessed, it is escalated to the sponsor, a resolution is agreed (using change control if the baseline changes) and it is tracked to closure.

n.0: The impact must be assessed before escalation so the sponsor has the information needed to decide.
n.1: An issue breaches tolerance, so the resolution is agreed with the sponsor after escalation, not before.
n.3: The issue must be logged before it is assessed, and it cannot be closed before a resolution is agreed.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A stakeholder demands that an issue be escalated before any assessment has been made. What should the project manager do?
o: Close the issue without recording any further detail
Assign the issue to a team member without logging it
Analyse the issue first to decide whether escalation is needed
Escalate the issue immediately as the stakeholder requests
Risk & Issue Management.w: The issue should be analysed first so the project manager can judge whether it genuinely exceeds project authority and warrants escalation.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What takes place during the closure stage of the issue management process?
o: Assignment of ownership to a responsible person
Formal verification and sign-off that the issue is resolved
Implementation of the corrective action needed
Initial logging of the issue when it is first identified
Risk & Issue Management.w: Closure confirms and records that the issue has been resolved, with the necessary verification and sign-off completed.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following is typically recorded during the closure stage of issue resolution?
o: The stakeholder responsibility matrix for the project
The proposed escalation route for the issue
The date the issue was resolved and the actions taken
The estimated likelihood of the issue recurring later
Risk & Issue Management.w: At closure the resolution date and a summary of the actions taken are recorded to confirm the issue is complete.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A product fails final testing because of a missed requirement, so the project manager formally records and recognises it. Which stage of issue resolution is this?
o: Closure
Analysis
Identification
Resolution
Risk & Issue Management.w: Formally recording and recognising the issue is the identification stage, which begins the resolution process.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following is NOT a standard step in the issue resolution process?
o: Analysis
Closure
Rescheduling
Identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: Rescheduling may be a consequence of resolving an issue but is not itself a formal step in the issue resolution process, which runs from identification to closure.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project's approval board is asked to decide how to resolve an issue affecting several workstreams. This situation best represents:
o: Issue escalation
Scope management
Risk reassessment
Stakeholder mapping
Risk & Issue Management.w: When an issue exceeds the project team's authority and is referred upward for a decision, this is issue escalation.

Risk & Issue Management.q: At what point in the issue resolution process are actions assigned to named owners?
o: When the issue is first identified and logged
When the issue's impact is first being assessed
When the resolution is agreed with the sponsor
When the issue is tracked through to its closure
Risk & Issue Management.w: Once the issue has been escalated, the sponsor and project manager agree the resolution and assign the actions needed to carry it out.

n.0: Logging captures the issue; the actions are not yet known at this point.
n.1: Assessment works out the impact; the response has not yet been agreed.
n.3: Tracking to closure follows the actions that were assigned when the resolution was agreed.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the main purpose of risk management on a project?
o: To improve the chance of meeting objectives by managing uncertainty
To replace the need for a project management plan
To transfer all responsibility for the project to the sponsor
To eliminate every possible risk before the project begins
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management aims to increase the likelihood of achieving objectives by identifying and responding to uncertainty, not to remove all risk.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why do projects undertake risk management?
o: To identify and respond to threats and opportunities proactively
To guarantee that no issues will ever arise during delivery
To ensure risks are only considered once the project has closed
To avoid having to communicate with project stakeholders
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management is a proactive process to identify, assess and respond to both threats and opportunities throughout the project.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does effective risk management benefit a project?
o: It shifts every decision onto the individual team members
It reduces the impact of threats and helps exploit opportunities
It removes all uncertainty from the project environment
It allows the project to ignore its business case
Risk & Issue Management.w: Managing risk reduces the effect of threats and helps the project take advantage of opportunities, improving the chance of success.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager maintains a risk management process throughout delivery. What is this mainly intended to achieve?
o: Better-informed decisions by anticipating and managing uncertainty
The removal of any need for quality management
A permanent record of every completed project activity
A reduction in the total number of project stakeholders
Risk & Issue Management.w: Ongoing risk management supports informed decision-making by anticipating uncertainty and planning responses.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Complete the statement: in APM terms, an issue is a problem that...
o: ...may or may not happen at some later point in the future
...has been broken down into smaller work packages
...breaches, or will soon breach, delegated tolerances
...marks the planned end of a stage of the project
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is a problem that is breaching, or about to breach, the delegated tolerances for the work and needs the sponsor's support to agree a resolution.

n.0: Something that may or may not happen is uncertain, which makes it a risk.
n.1: Breaking work into packages describes the work breakdown structure.
n.3: A point marking the end of a stage is a milestone or decision gate.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does an issue differ from a risk?
o: An issue is uncertain; a risk is certain to occur
An issue affects only cost; a risk affects only time
An issue is always positive; a risk is always negative
An issue has already happened; a risk may happen in future
Risk & Issue Management.w: By definition an issue has already occurred, whereas a risk is an uncertain future event.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A supplier has failed to deliver a critical component, halting project work. How should this be classified?
o: An issue, because the problem has already occurred
A milestone, because it marks a point in the schedule
An assumption, because it was expected during planning
A risk, because it might affect the project later
Risk & Issue Management.w: A problem that has already happened and is affecting the project is an issue, not a risk.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement about project issues is correct?
o: They are potential future events recorded in a risk register
They are always resolved by the project manager acting alone
They can only arise after a project has formally closed
They need the sponsor's support as they exceed tolerances
Risk & Issue Management.w: Because an issue breaches, or is about to breach, delegated tolerances, it is beyond the project manager's authority and needs the sponsor's support to agree a resolution.

n.0: Potential future events are risks; issues are happening now and go in the issue log.
n.1: Problems the project manager can solve within tolerance are not issues in the APM sense; issues are escalated.
n.2: Issues arise during the project; after closure there is no project to manage them.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A risk recorded earlier in the project has now actually happened. In project terminology, what has it become?
o: A milestone
A constraint
An issue
An assumption
Risk & Issue Management.w: When a risk materialises it becomes an issue: a problem that has occurred and now requires management action.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why does an identified project issue demand immediate management attention rather than monitoring alone?
o: Because it is a problem that has already occurred and is affecting the project
Because it is a constraint that was fixed at the project's outset
Because it is an uncertain event that has not yet happened
Because it is a benefit expected only after the project closes
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue has already occurred and is affecting the project, so it demands action now, unlike a risk which is only monitored as a possibility.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A lead engineer resigns unexpectedly, work on their deliverables stops, and the delay now exceeds the schedule tolerance agreed with the sponsor. How is this best classified?
o: An assumption
A dependency
An issue
A risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: The event has happened and breaches the agreed tolerance, so it is an issue that must be escalated to the sponsor for a resolution.

n.0: An assumption is something taken to be true for planning purposes, not a problem that has occurred.
n.1: A dependency is a link between activities or deliverables, not an event that has happened.
n.3: A risk is uncertain and in the future; the resignation and delay have already happened.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Where would a project manager typically record and track a problem that has already arisen during delivery?
o: In the business case
In the communication plan
In the risk register
In the issue log
Risk & Issue Management.w: A problem that has arisen is an issue and is recorded and tracked in the issue log, distinct from the risk register used for potential events.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Delivered equipment has arrived damaged and cannot be installed, stopping the next task. Why is this an issue rather than a risk?
o: Because it relates purely to a much later delivery phase
Because it is at this stage still only a future possibility
Because it has already happened and is now impacting delivery
Because it has no measurable effect on the project at all
Risk & Issue Management.w: The event has occurred and is affecting the project now, which makes it an issue; a risk would still only be a potential event.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Considering how projects define their terms, which of the following situations most clearly represents an issue?
o: A supplier might raise its component prices next quarter
A required approval has been refused, halting the next stage
A team member may possibly leave before delivery ends
Bad weather could delay some outdoor work later in delivery
Risk & Issue Management.w: A refused approval that has halted progress has already happened, making it an issue; the others are uncertain future events, or risks.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A new starter asks what separates an issue from an assumption in project terms. Which explanation is correct?
o: An issue is a problem that has occurred; an assumption is something taken to be true for planning
An issue and an assumption mean effectively the same thing
An issue is a future possibility; an assumption is a current problem
An issue is a benefit; an assumption is a cost to be recovered
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is a problem that has already occurred, whereas an assumption is something accepted as true for planning purposes; they are different concepts.

Risk & Issue Management.q: The project's actual spend has now exceeded its approved budget and finance has flagged it. How is this best classified?
o: An issue
A dependency
A tolerance
A risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: A confirmed overspend that has already happened and needs action is an issue, not a risk, which remains only a possibility.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement correctly reflects how a project issue should be treated once it has been identified?
o: It must be actively managed and resolved, and escalated where necessary
It should be ignored until it possibly occurs at some later point
It should be recorded only within the project's risk register
It should be treated as a guaranteed benefit for the project
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is a current problem requiring active management, resolution and, where appropriate, escalation; it is not a future or beneficial event.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which word most accurately captures the essential nature of a project risk?
o: Certainty
Milestone
Uncertainty
Deliverable
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is fundamentally an uncertain event, distinguishing it from certainties, deliverables or milestones.

Risk & Issue Management.q: According to APM terminology, a risk may have what kind of effect on project objectives?
o: Only a negative effect, never a positive one
No effect on objectives whatsoever
A guaranteed effect that is always realised
Either a positive or a negative effect
Risk & Issue Management.w: APM defines risk as covering both threats and opportunities, so its effect may be negative or positive.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which two elements together characterise a risk when it is first defined on a project?
o: Its uncertainty of occurring and its potential effect on objectives
Its exact cost and its confirmed completion date
Its assigned owner and its reporting frequency
Its approval status and its version number
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk combines uncertainty of occurrence with a potential effect on objectives, unlike a certainty or fixed fact.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why is a risk described as 'uncertain' rather than definite?
o: Because it is always guaranteed to occur eventually
Because it may or may not happen in the future
Because it has already happened and been recorded
Because it can never affect the project's objectives
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk carries uncertainty: it is a possible future event that may or may not materialise.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A positive risk that could benefit the project if it occurs is often referred to as which of the following?
o: An opportunity
A threat
An issue
A constraint
Risk & Issue Management.w: In APM terms a positive risk is an opportunity, whereas a negative risk is a threat.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does a risk differ from an assumption on a project?
o: A risk has occurred; an assumption cannot occur
There is no difference between the two terms
A risk is always true; an assumption is always false
A risk is an uncertain future event; an assumption is taken to be true
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is an uncertain event that might happen, while an assumption is something accepted as true for planning.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of these statements describes a genuine project risk rather than a current problem?
o: A team member resigned from the project last week
The budget was exceeded during the last reporting period
A supplier has already failed to deliver essential materials
Adverse weather might delay outdoor work next month
Risk & Issue Management.w: Only the weather statement is an uncertain future event; the others have already occurred and are issues.

Risk & Issue Management.q: In APM terms, the potential of an event to affect the achievement of objectives is known as what?
o: A benefit
An issue
A dependency
A risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk is the potential of an event or situation to affect the achievement of objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement about the definition of risk is correct?
o: Risk relates only to events that are certain to happen
Risk describes events that have already occurred and been logged
Risk can encompass both threats and opportunities to objectives
Risk applies only to the financial aspects of a project
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk is uncertain and, in APM usage, includes both threats and opportunities across all project objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Issue management differs from risk management chiefly because it deals with what?
o: The measurement of benefits after handover
The decomposition of deliverables into work packages
Problems that have already arisen and now need resolving
Uncertain events that have not yet happened
Risk & Issue Management.w: Issue management addresses problems that have already occurred, whereas risk management handles uncertain future events.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why is a structured issue management process valuable to a project manager?
o: It ensures problems are logged, assessed and resolved consistently
It fixes the project scope so no changes are ever needed
It guarantees the project will finish under budget
It replaces the need for a risk register entirely
Risk & Issue Management.w: A structured process ensures issues are captured, evaluated and resolved in a consistent, controlled way.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Within issue management, what is the purpose of having a defined escalation route?
o: To decompose the project's scope into work packages
To raise problems beyond the manager's authority to those who can resolve them
To identify uncertain events long before they occur
To measure the benefits delivered after project closure
Risk & Issue Management.w: An escalation route lets issues beyond the project manager's authority reach those who can resolve them.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project without any issue management process is most likely to experience which of the following?
o: An automatic improvement in team morale
A guaranteed increase in delivered benefits
A permanent reduction in all project risks
Unresolved problems that grow and threaten objectives
Risk & Issue Management.w: Without issue management, problems go unaddressed and can escalate to threaten the project's objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why does an effective issue management process assign a clear owner to each logged issue?
o: So that the issue is reclassified as a future risk
So that no record of the issue needs to be kept
So that the issue can be ignored until the project closes
So that responsibility for resolving the issue is unambiguous and it is progressed
Risk & Issue Management.w: Assigning an owner makes resolution responsibility unambiguous, ensuring the issue is actively progressed to closure.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager introduces an issue log and escalation route. What purpose does this primarily serve?
o: It records the estimated cost of each work package
It sets the acceptance criteria for the final product
It ensures current problems are captured and dealt with promptly
It forecasts uncertain events that may occur later
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue log and escalation route ensure current problems are captured and resolved promptly, the aim of issue management.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement best reflects a purpose of risk management that goes beyond simply avoiding threats?
o: It removes all uncertainty from the project
It also identifies and helps exploit potential opportunities
It guarantees the project will finish under budget
It transfers accountability for outcomes to suppliers
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management addresses uncertainty in both directions, seeking to exploit opportunities as well as reduce threats.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why is risk management considered a proactive discipline throughout the delivery of a project?
o: It anticipates and addresses uncertainty before it affects objectives
It records lessons learned solely at project closure
It focuses purely on logging issues after they occur
It only reacts once problems have already materialised
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management is proactive because it identifies and responds to uncertainty before it can affect project objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: In what way does an effective risk management process improve decision-making on a project?
o: It removes uncertainty so no judgement is required
It provides a structured understanding of threats and opportunities to inform choices
It ensures decisions are only made at project closure
It replaces the need for a project board to make decisions
Risk & Issue Management.w: By assessing threats and opportunities, risk management gives decision-makers a structured basis for informed choices.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project team meets regularly to review threats and plan responses before they occur. What core purpose of risk management does this serve?
o: Guaranteeing that the original plan will never change
Transferring all responsibility for outcomes to the sponsor
Reducing the impact of uncertainty on project objectives
Recording issues only after they have disrupted delivery
Risk & Issue Management.w: Regularly reviewing and responding to threats in advance reduces the impact of uncertainty on the project's objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager reviews risks at every team meeting rather than only at the outset. What benefit does this ongoing review bring?
o: It guarantees that no risks will materialise during delivery
It removes the need to maintain a risk register
It transfers all accountability for risks to the sponsor
It provides early warning of new and changing risks so responses stay current
Risk & Issue Management.w: Reviewing risks regularly gives early warning of new and changing risks, keeping planned responses current throughout delivery.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A team identifies that early supplier delivery could let them finish sooner and plans to take advantage. Which purpose of risk management does this show?
o: Exploiting opportunities as well as managing threats
Recording issues after they have already occurred
Avoiding the need to update the risk register
Eliminating all uncertainty from the schedule
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management addresses positive uncertainty too, so planning to capture a beneficial outcome is exploiting an opportunity.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement best corrects the misconception that risk management removes all risk from a project?
o: It ensures no threats will ever materialise
It guarantees the project will meet every objective
It transfers every risk to an external supplier
It manages uncertainty to acceptable levels rather than removing it entirely
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management reduces and controls uncertainty to acceptable levels; it cannot eliminate all risk from a project.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How can a well-run risk management process increase stakeholder confidence in a project?
o: By removing the need for any progress reporting
By promising that no risks will ever occur
By showing threats are being identified and actively managed
By hiding potential threats from the project board
Risk & Issue Management.w: Demonstrating that risks are being systematically identified and managed reassures stakeholders that the project is under control.

Risk & Issue Management.q: An organisation with strong risk management is more likely to achieve its project objectives. Why is this the case?
o: Risk management removes the need for a project sponsor
Uncertainty is actively managed, improving the chance objectives are met
Risk management guarantees delivery below the approved budget
Risk management removes every possible threat before it can occur
Risk & Issue Management.w: Actively managing uncertainty improves the likelihood that the project's objectives are achieved.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A data breach has just occurred and is disrupting the project. In risk terminology, how is this event now best classified?
o: An assumption, because it was anticipated
A constraint, because it limits the project
An issue, because it has already occurred and requires action
A risk, because it might affect the project
Risk & Issue Management.w: An event that has already occurred and is affecting the project is an issue requiring resolution, not a future uncertainty.

Risk & Issue Management.q: The team records that adverse weather might delay outdoor work next month. How is this best classified?
o: A change, because it alters the agreed scope
An issue, because it is affecting delivery now
A risk, because it is uncertain and may occur in future
A constraint, because it limits the schedule
Risk & Issue Management.w: An uncertain future event that may or may not happen is a risk, distinguishing it from an issue that has occurred.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Unlike an issue, what defining feature does a risk always carry on a project?
o: An effect that has already been felt by the team
A guaranteed negative effect on the budget
A degree of uncertainty about whether it will occur
A requirement for immediate corrective action now
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk always carries uncertainty about whether it will occur, unlike an issue which has already happened.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why does a risk require a different management response from an issue?
o: A risk is owned by suppliers and an issue by customers
A risk is recorded but an issue is deliberately ignored
A risk affects benefits while an issue never does
A risk needs planned responses in case it occurs; an issue needs action now
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is managed through planned responses ahead of time, whereas an issue has occurred and requires immediate resolution.

Risk & Issue Management.q: One event may happen next quarter; another has already stopped work today. How should each be classified respectively?
o: Both as risks, since both affect the project
The first as a risk; the second as an issue
The first as an issue; the second as a risk
Both as issues, since both are recorded
Risk & Issue Management.w: A possible future event is a risk; one that has already occurred and stopped work is an issue.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which pairing correctly matches the terms 'risk' and 'issue' to their defining feature?
o: Risk = might occur; issue = has occurred
Risk = has occurred; issue = might occur
Risk = external only; issue = internal only
Risk = certain benefit; issue = certain threat
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is a possible future event that might occur, whereas an issue is something that has already happened.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which sequence best represents the stages of a typical risk management process?
o: Logging, escalation, resolution and reporting
Identification, assessment, response and closure
Planning, execution, monitoring and closure
Concept, definition, delivery and handover
Risk & Issue Management.w: A typical risk management process runs from identification, through assessment (analysis) and response, to closure.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager reviews a checklist of common threats to spot what could affect the project. Which stage of risk management is this?
o: Risk response
Risk analysis
Risk identification
Risk closure
Risk & Issue Management.w: Using prompt lists or checklists to find potential threats is part of the risk identification stage.

Risk & Issue Management.q: During which stage of the risk management process are risks assessed for probability and impact so that they can be prioritised?
o: Identification
Analysis
Response
Closure
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk analysis assesses probability and impact, enabling risks to be prioritised for attention.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Having assessed its risks, a team decides how to treat each one, choosing to reduce, transfer, avoid or accept. Which stage is this?
o: Risk analysis
Risk identification
Risk response
Risk closure
Risk & Issue Management.w: Deciding how to treat each risk — reduce, transfer, avoid or accept — is the risk response stage.

Risk & Issue Management.q: At the closure stage of the risk management process, what does a team typically do with a risk that can no longer occur?
o: Formally close it and capture any lessons learned
Reassess its probability and impact scores
Transfer it to an external supplier under contract
Escalate it to the programme board for a decision
Risk & Issue Management.w: At closure a risk that can no longer occur is formally closed and any lessons are recorded for future use.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does the risk analysis stage differ from the risk identification stage?
o: Identification assesses probability and impact, whereas analysis simply lists the risks
Both stages only find risks, but identification also selects the responses
Both stages only assess impact, but analysis is done after closure
Identification finds the risks, whereas analysis assesses their probability and impact
Risk & Issue Management.w: Identification discovers and records the risks; analysis then evaluates each one's probability and impact so they can be prioritised.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager puts an agreed contingency arrangement into action and monitors whether it is working. Which part of the process is this?
o: Closing the risk register
Identifying new risks
Implementing the risk responses
Analysing the risk's probability
Risk & Issue Management.w: Carrying out and monitoring the agreed responses is part of implementing the risk responses within the process.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why is risk analysis carried out before deciding on responses in the risk management process?
o: So that the project budget can be finalised and fixed
So that the responses can be chosen at random for fairness
So that every identified risk can be immediately closed
So effort can be focused on the most significant risks first
Risk & Issue Management.w: Analysis prioritises risks by probability and impact so that responses target the most significant threats.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Midway through delivery a team spots a new threat that was not previously listed. Which stage does the process return to?
o: Closure
Analysis
Response
Identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: Risk management is iterative; a newly spotted threat re-enters the process at the identification stage before being analysed and responded to.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A newly logged issue has just been assessed for its impact. What happens at the next stage of the process?
o: It is logged in the issue register for the first time
It is tracked to closure and the lessons are captured
Its probability of occurring is analysed and scored
It is escalated to the sponsor to agree a resolution
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is, by definition, breaching or about to breach tolerance, so after assessment it is escalated to the sponsor, who agrees the resolution.

n.0: Logging is the first stage and has already happened.
n.1: Tracking to closure is the final stage, after a resolution has been agreed.
n.2: Probability scoring applies to risks; an issue has already happened, so it is certain.

Risk & Issue Management.q: After logging an issue, the project manager works out how seriously it affects cost, time and quality. Which stage of issue resolution is this?
o: Closure
Identification
Assessment
Escalation
Risk & Issue Management.w: Determining the effect of a logged issue on the project's objectives is the assessment stage.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why is the closure stage important within the issue resolution process?
o: It assigns the issue to an owner for the very first time
It confirms the issue is resolved and records any lessons learned
It decides whether the issue should be escalated further
It determines the issue's likely impact on the schedule
Risk & Issue Management.w: Closure confirms the issue has been dealt with and captures lessons that may help on future work.

Risk & Issue Management.q: An issue is beyond the project manager's authority to resolve, so it is referred to the sponsor. Which stage of the process is this?
o: Assessment
Closure
Escalation
Identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: Referring an issue to a higher authority when it exceeds the manager's remit is the escalation stage.

Risk & Issue Management.q: The team agrees and carries out corrective actions to remove the effect of a logged issue. Which stage of issue resolution does this describe?
o: Logging
Escalation
Resolution
Identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: Agreeing and carrying out the corrective actions to deal with the issue is the resolution stage.

Risk & Issue Management.q: As soon as a problem is confirmed to be affecting the project now, where is it first recorded in the resolution process?
o: In the business case during escalation
In the risk register during analysis
In the issue log at the identification stage
In the benefits plan at closure
Risk & Issue Management.w: A confirmed issue is first recorded in the issue log as part of the identification stage of the process.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A project manager keeps a single document listing each risk, its owner and its planned response. What is this document?
o: The communication plan
The risk register
The quality plan
The business case
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk register is the central record of identified risks, their assessment, owners and planned responses, supporting ongoing risk management.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following would you normally expect to find recorded against each entry in a risk register?
o: The risk's probability, impact and planned response
The exact wording of the project's business case
The full technical specification of every deliverable
The behavioural role of the person raising it
Risk & Issue Management.w: Each register entry typically records the risk description, its probability and impact, a risk owner and the agreed response.

Risk & Issue Management.q: During a review, a project manager updates the status of several risks in the register. Why is keeping it current important?
o: It ensures decisions are based on up-to-date risk information
It guarantees no new risks will ever emerge
It removes the need to hold any further reviews
It transfers all risks to the project sponsor
Risk & Issue Management.w: A regularly updated register keeps risk information current, so responses and decisions reflect the project's actual exposure.

Risk & Issue Management.q: How does a risk register support accountability within a project's risk management?
o: By removing the need to assign any risk owners
By assigning an owner responsible for each risk
By recording only risks that have already occurred
By listing the project's stakeholders and their interests
Risk & Issue Management.w: The register names a risk owner for each entry, making individuals accountable for monitoring and responding to their risks.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which statement best describes how a risk register is used across the life of a project?
o: It is a living document reviewed and updated throughout
It is completed once at initiation and then archived
It is produced only after the project has closed
It is used solely to record issues that have occurred
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk register is a living document, reviewed and updated throughout delivery as risks change, close or newly emerge.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A newly identified threat to the schedule needs capturing. Where should the project manager record it and its planned response?
o: In the quality plan
In the risk register
In the communication plan
In the business case
Risk & Issue Management.w: Newly identified risks, with their assessment and planned responses, are captured in the risk register.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Why does a risk register support effective communication about risk on a project?
o: It provides a shared, consistent record all parties can reference
It records only the risks the sponsor wishes to see
It hides risk information from the wider stakeholders
It replaces the need for any progress reporting
Risk & Issue Management.w: By holding risk information in one consistent place, the register gives stakeholders a shared reference for discussing and reviewing risk.

Risk & Issue Management.q: After a response reduces a risk's likelihood, what should happen to that entry in the risk register?
o: It should be updated to reflect its revised assessment
It should be deleted immediately from the register
It should be moved into the project's issue log
It should be left unchanged to preserve the original
Risk & Issue Management.w: The register is updated so that the revised probability and residual exposure are recorded, keeping the risk picture accurate.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical use of a risk register?
o: Authorising payments to the project's suppliers
Providing a basis for reviewing risks at meetings
Tracking the status and ownership of identified risks
Recording the agreed response for each risk
Risk & Issue Management.w: The register manages information about risks; authorising supplier payments is a financial and procurement matter, not a register function.

Risk & Issue Management.q: In the context of project management, how is the term 'risk' best defined?
o: A deliverable that has been completed and formally accepted
A certain event that will definitely disrupt the project's objectives
A problem that has already occurred and now requires resolution
An uncertain event that, if it occurs, could affect objectives positively or negatively
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk is an uncertain future event or set of circumstances that, should it occur, would have an effect on the achievement of objectives.

Risk & Issue Management.q: What is the main purpose of a risk register on a project?
o: To allocate the project's budget across its individual work packages
To record identified risks together with their analysis, responses and current status
To define the agreed boundaries of the project's scope of work
To list the project's milestones and their planned completion dates
Risk & Issue Management.w: A risk register documents each identified risk with its assessment, planned response and status, supporting ongoing monitoring and control.

Risk & Issue Management.q: A key supplier unexpectedly ceases trading during delivery. How should this now be classified?
o: A risk, because it remains an uncertain future possibility
An opportunity, because it is likely to benefit the project
A change request, because it alters the project's agreed scope
An issue, because the uncertain event has now actually occurred
Risk & Issue Management.w: An issue is an event that has occurred and now requires management action, whereas a risk is still an uncertain future possibility.

Risk & Issue Management.q: You find the same fault recurring in every test cycle. Which process should be used to log and resolve it?
o: Quality planning
Risk identification
Scope definition
Issue management
Risk & Issue Management.w: Issue management logs, tracks and resolves problems that have already occurred and are affecting the project.

Risk & Issue Management.q: Which stage of a typical risk management process involves implementing and reviewing the agreed responses to risks?
o: Analysis
Closure
Response
Identification
Risk & Issue Management.w: The response stage puts the planned actions into effect and reviews their outcome, adjusting them as the risk exposure changes.

Quality.q: A project manager describes a deliverable as being of 'high quality'. What does 'quality' mean in the context of a project?
o: That it meets the agreed requirements and is fit for purpose
That it was completed ahead of its planned schedule
That it includes more features than were originally specified
That it exceeds recognised industry standards for the sector
Quality.w: In APM terms, quality means the deliverable conforms to its agreed requirements and is fit for its intended purpose.

Quality.q: What is meant by 'quality' in the context of a project?
o: Delivering outputs that meet the agreed requirements and are fit for purpose
Providing the most technically advanced solution available
Meeting customer expectations regardless of the agreed scope
Completing every task well ahead of its planned deadline
Quality.w: Quality is defined as meeting the specified requirements and ensuring the output is fit for its intended purpose.

Quality.q: A client receives a product that looks impressive but fails to meet several contractual requirements. How would its quality be assessed?
o: It is high quality, because of its technical complexity
It is high quality, because it exceeded the client's expectations
It is low quality, because it does not meet the agreed requirements
It is acceptable quality, because the client was impressed by it
Quality.w: Quality is judged against the agreed requirements, so a product that fails to meet them is of low quality regardless of its appearance.

Quality.q: Why is it important that project outputs are fit for purpose?
o: To impress stakeholders during the project's review meetings
To shorten the overall duration of the project's activities
To meet quality objectives and deliver value to the customer
To reduce the planning resources needed by the project
Quality.w: Outputs that are fit for purpose satisfy the project's quality objectives and deliver the intended value to the customer.

Quality.q: A project team is discussing whether their final product meets the definition of 'quality'. Which statement best defines quality?
o: Every project risk was successfully avoided during delivery
The final cost of the product came in below the initial budget
The deliverable includes as many additional features as possible
The output meets the defined requirements and serves its intended purpose
Quality.w: Quality means the deliverable satisfies its agreed specifications and is suitable for its intended use.

Quality.q: A project manager sets up processes to ensure the final product meets the agreed requirements. What is the main purpose of quality management?
o: To make the project's procurement arrangements simpler
To reduce the number of stakeholders involved in the project
To ensure outputs are delivered to a consistent and acceptable standard
To increase the overall speed at which the product is delivered
Quality.w: Quality management exists to ensure that project outputs consistently meet the agreed standards and are fit for purpose.

Quality.q: Why is it beneficial for a project to establish its quality management approach right at the start?
o: To ensure outputs meet requirements and are fit for purpose
To deliver the project in the shortest time possible
To transfer all quality responsibility across to the suppliers
To remove the need for any project documentation later
Quality.w: A quality management approach set from the outset helps ensure deliverables meet the required standards and are fit for purpose throughout the life cycle.
